acceptedAnswer.text: Online reputation management is the work of making sure the ratings, reviews and profiles people find about you are accurate, current and a fair picture of your business.

mainEntity.name: How does online reputation management work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We audit what people see, help you ask real customers, parents and students for honest reviews, reply to every review, keep profiles accurate and report on what changes.

mainEntity.name: What does online reputation management cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A monthly scope, agreed after a call. It is written down so you can see what each month covers. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your site, your market and how much you want done.
No. We cannot promise to remove reviews or lift a rating, and genuine reviews stay. We commit to honest replies, real review requests and clear reporting. We never write or buy reviews.

mainEntity.name: Who is online reputation management for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Education brands, B2B companies and D2C brands whose buyers check reviews first. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on contribution margin and repeat purchase, B2B on the cost of a qualified lead, education on enquiries, visits and admissions.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Access to your review and business profiles, your customer or student contact process, and a person who can approve replies.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: Buyers, parents and students check you before they contact you. Each stage below is a place that check can go wrong, and the work that prevents it.

stages.breaks: Not knowing what people find when they search your name.
stages.why: Most people look you up before they enquire. If you have never checked what shows up, you are guessing at the first impression.
stages.does: We audit your ratings, reviews, profiles and search results across Google, review sites and social, and show you what a prospective customer sees.

stages.breaks: Hoping happy customers will leave reviews on their own.
stages.why: Unhappy customers are more likely to post unprompted, so a few loud complaints can outweigh many quiet, satisfied customers.
stages.does: We set up simple, honest ways to ask genuine customers, parents and students for a review at the right moment, within each platform's rules.

stages.breaks: Leaving reviews unanswered, or answering defensively.
stages.why: A reply is read by everyone who reads the review. A calm, specific answer shows how you treat people when something goes wrong.
stages.does: We draft and manage replies to positive and negative reviews in your voice, and pass genuine problems to your team to resolve.

stages.breaks: Old hours, wrong phone numbers and half-filled profiles.
stages.why: Out-of-date or inconsistent information across listings makes a business look careless, and sends people to the wrong place.
stages.does: We keep your profiles and listings accurate and consistent, with current photos, contact details and answers to common questions.

stages.breaks: Finding out about a problem weeks after it started.
stages.why: Reputation changes gradually, then suddenly. Without regular reporting, a fall in rating or a new theme of complaints goes unnoticed.
stages.does: We monitor ratings and reviews and report monthly on rating, review volume, response time and the themes behind what people say.
